question.problem:
Find the equation of the osculating plane (in parametric form) for the curve $r(t)$ at the point where $t=0$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+{t}^{3}\,k,\,T(0)=i,\,N(0)=j.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The osculating plane passes through the point that is at the tip of the vector $r(0).$ The vectors $T(0)$ and $N(0)$ are parallel to this plane. Therefore, the equation of the plane (in parametric form) can be written as

$$
R(s,u)=r(0)+s\,T(0)+u\,N(0),\,s,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

 

We have that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =0\,i+{0}^{2}\,j+{0}^{3}\,k=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the equation of the osculating plane at the point $(0,0,0)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s,u) & =r(0)+s\,T(0)+u\,N(0) \\  & =0+s(i)+u(j) \\  & =s\,i+u\,j.\end{aligned}
$$
